subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Roads: Paths That Lasted 2,000 Years
description: A micro-lesson that makes Roman Roads: Paths That Lasted 2,000 Years usable.

hook.text: Roman roads were so well built that some are still in use today, 2,000 years after construction.

buildup.text: The road network spanned 250,000 miles — enough to circle Earth ten times. It connected every corner of the empire.

discovery.text: Roads were built in layers: rubble base, gravel fill, and fitted paving stones, all crowned for drainage.

twist.text: Many modern European highways follow the exact routes of Roman roads. The empire's planners chose the best paths first.

climax.text: Scholars mapped every known Roman road digitally. The network looks like a modern transit map with Rome at the hub.

punchline.text: All roads led to Rome. Many of them still do.

quiz.question: How large was the Roman road network at its peak?
options: About 50,000 miles connecting major cities only
Around 250,000 miles — enough to circle Earth ten times
Over 1 million miles including unpaved paths
